case.case_title: Sirisena and Others v. Earnest Perera and Others
case.source_citation: Supreme Court of Sri Lanka, S.C. Application No. 14/90, decided on 7 and 8 May 1991

clause.text: No citizen shall be discriminated against on the grounds of race, religion, language, caste, sex, political opinion, place of birth or any one of such grounds.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the Petitioners were discriminated against on prohibited grounds in violation of Article 12(2).
case_context.petitioner_claim: The Petitioners alleged unlawful arrest and detention but did not specifically claim discrimination on grounds listed in Article 12(2).
case_context.respondent_argument: The Respondents denied unlawful detention and did not address discrimination claims under Article 12(2).
key_facts: Petitioners were detained and allegedly mistreated by police during investigation of a fatal accident.
No evidence or argument was presented regarding discrimination based on race, religion, language, caste, sex, political opinion, or place of birth.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The Court did not materially engage with Article 12(2) as there was no substantive claim or evidence of discrimination on the prohibited grounds.
reasoning.application_to_facts: Since no discrimination claim was made or argued, the Court did not apply or interpret Article 12(2) in relation to the facts.

outcome.holding: No finding of infringement or violation of Article 12(2) was made.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 12(2) was not materially engaged or central to the Court's reasoning or outcome in this case.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The Petitioners' claims and the Court's findings focused on unlawful arrest and detention without any allegation or evidence of discrimination on grounds listed in Article 12(2).
